items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Bubber and Tricky would turn it around. We still played sweet music but we -- little by little it come to the growl and things, you know, because Tricky growled and Bubber growled

ctx.x: Duke Ellington said once that there was -- he was attempting to get the guys to change the name of the music from jazz to Negro music when you all got to New York. Do you remember that?
No. No, that never come up. What did

come up, the real truth about it, we played -- I don't know how it originated or nothing like that, but somebody -- I don't know whether it was Paul Whiteman because he idolized Duke or Gershwin. He was a steady customer at the Cotton Club.
